evidence.says: Attributes The European Free-Trade Association: an analysis of "The outer seven" to Frederick Victor Meyer.
Lists Frederick Victor Meyer, University of Exeter, as the author of a 1982 review.
Lists Freeman William Meyer among graduate scholars in History; BA, University of Kansas, 1942; MA, University of Connecticut, 1949.
Identifies Freeman W. Meyer as a Cornell PhD of 1951.

basis: The LC book is attributed to Frederick Victor Meyer, whose published review gives a University of Exeter affiliation. Cornell records identify the candidate as Freeman William Meyer, a History graduate scholar and PhD of 1951, supporting a different person.

evidence.says: Thomas J. Kuehn has a Chicago PhD (1977), joined Clemson in 1981, and wrote Emancipation in Late Medieval Florence (1982) and Law, Family, and Women (1991).
The December 2004 review of Matthew Stibbe, Women in the Third Reich, credits Thomas J. Kuehn at the Strassler Family Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies, Clark University.

basis: The LC books belong to Clemson's Thomas J. Kuehn, but candidate p-184898 is anchored only to a review credited to that name at Clark's Strassler Center. No source found links that review credit to the Clemson author or securely establishes a different person.

evidence.says: The review of Aldus Manutius (1995) identifies its author Martin Davies as head of the Incunabula Short Title Catalogue at the British Library.
Martin Davies is Emeritus Reader at Leicester; his books include Identity or History? (1995), Historics (2006) and Imprisoned by History (2010).
Identifies Martin Leonard Davies as a Leicester academic for 35 years, first in French and German and later History, and author of Imprisoned by History.

basis: The LC-listed Aldus Manutius is tied to the British Library catalogue head. Candidate p-181316 is the Leicester academic Martin Leonard Davies, identified by a different institutional career and the books Historics and Imprisoned by History; the evidence indicates distinct authors.

evidence.says: Lists Self-Determination and History in the Third World under David C. Gordon; gives no degree or dissertation information.

basis: The publisher lists an LC book under David C. Gordon but supplies no link to the candidate’s 1958 Princeton dissertation, A Philosophe Views the French Revolution: The Abbe Morellet (1727-1819).
